title: Move git identity out of tracked git/.gitconfig into ~/.gitconfig.local
description: git/.gitconfig (symlinked as ~/.gitconfig) currently has uncommitted user.name=R0SEWT-CGIAR and user.email=rody.vilchez@cgiar.org. The repo convention (README) is that the tracked .gitconfig excludes identity; it belongs in ~/.gitconfig.local. Committing it would leak a real email to a public repo. Fix: create/populate ~/.gitconfig.local with the identity, then git checkout git/.gitconfig to drop the tracked change.

title: Fix invisible Zoroak actor on GNOME Shell 46

acceptance_criteria: Stow link and PNG validated; static and animated states visible at 1920x1200; idle, working, review, failure, and roaaak respond within one second; no GNOME Shell errors; changes committed and pushed to PR branch.

title: Zoroak: hot-reload animations from external JSON manifest
description: Let the extension read the timeline table (sequence/frameMs/loop/next per state, plus aliases) from animations.json in the extension dir, watched by a Gio file monitor like the state file. Editing the JSON re-applies animations live with no shell reload/logout. Keep the in-code STATES/ALIASES as fallback defaults; merge manifest onto defaults; ignore invalid/partial JSON (keep last-good) so an in-progress edit never crashes the shell. Deploying the manifest-reading extension.js needs one logout; after that all animation tuning is hot.
close_reason: Verified live in a nested shell: editing animations.json (idle 180->600ms) slowed the fox instantly, no logout. Hot-reload + validation working.

title: Zoroak: timeline animation engine (sequences, per-frame timing, transitions)
description: Replace the fixed linear frame loop (frame = (frame+1) % frames at a global 150ms interval) with a timeline engine that supports: per-state frame sequences (arrays of column indices, enabling pauses and ping-pong without new art), per-state frame duration (frameMs), loop vs one-shot playback, and next-state transitions for one-shot actions (wave/jump/roaaak -> idle). Keep the current 7x9 atlas so no new art is needed yet. This is the foundation so future longer/richer animations drop in via config, not by rewriting the extension.
close_reason: Confirmed working after session restart: click-through + timeline engine (roaaak plays once and returns to idle, idle ping-pong).

title: Zoroak blocks clicks to windows underneath
description: The companion widget is added to GNOME Shell chrome with affectsInputRegion:true and reactive:true, so its bounding rectangle captures all pointer clicks (even over transparent sprite pixels), preventing clicks from reaching the window/desktop beneath it. Make it click-through (affectsInputRegion:false, non-reactive) and move the hide feature from right-click to a zoroakctl hide/show command.
close_reason: Confirmed working after session restart: click-through + timeline engine (roaaak plays once and returns to idle, idle ping-pong).

value: Zoroak stays a custom GNOME Shell extension (not Shimeji/oneko/RunCat) on purpose: its unique value is being driven by an external state file via zoroakctl to mirror terminal/agent state (idle/working/review/failure). Off-the-shelf desktop pets don't take an external state signal cleanly. The timeline engine is intentionally minimal (~120 lines) glue, not a framework.
